sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: JBSA-Randolph is home to the 12th Flying Training Wing, whose training includes pilot instructor training (its combat systems officer training is at NAS Pensacola, Florida). The T-7A Red Hawk, which will replace the T-38C, is arriving: the third was delivered to Randolph on Aug. 25, 2026.
It also hosts the headquarters of Air Education and Training Command (AETC), the Air Force Personnel Center (AFPC) and the Air Force Recruiting Service.

source.label: 12th Flying Training Wing fact sheet; AETC (official)

sections.title: The Taj Mahal and a Historic Base

data.subtitle: Randolph is a flying-training base with a historic core, in the fast-growing suburbs northeast of San Antonio.
intro: Its best-known building is Building 100, the 'Taj Mahal': completed in 1931, 170 feet high and the tallest structure on base, with a working 500,000-gallon water tank in its tower. It houses the 12th Flying Training Wing's offices, at the heart of a 410-acre historic district of 398 structures built between 1929 and 1950.
The base sits in the Universal City and Schertz area northeast of San Antonio, among fast-growing suburbs: Census estimates show Cibolo up 20.9% and New Braunfels up 35.5% from 2020 to 2025.

recommendations.advice: Universal City, Schertz, Converse and Cibolo are 5 to 11 minutes from the base with no traffic. Town and school district lines don't match: Schertz-Cibolo-Universal City ISD and Judson ISD both list parts of Universal City, Schertz and Converse, so confirm the district for any address.

Randolph Field ISD (A, 94 in 2026) is on base. Children living on base attend automatically; others need an approved transfer, given by priority, limited by staffing and screened on grades, attendance and discipline.

Brooke Army Medical Center on Fort Sam Houston is about 25 minutes away and Wilford Hall on Lackland about 42 with no traffic, and JBSA's free base shuttles run on Lackland and Fort Sam Houston, not Randolph. TxDOT's I-35 work runs to 2027 on the central stretch and is planned for 2028 to 2032 farther north.

source.label: JBSA news: tour of JBSA-Randolph history (official)

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Only the Lindsey (Main) Gate is open 24 hours. The East Gate opens weekdays 6 to 8 a.m. inbound and 3 to 5 p.m. outbound, the West Gate weekdays (6 a.m. to 2 p.m. inbound, to 6 p.m. outbound), and the South Gate, also the commercial gate, weekdays 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. at Lower Seguin Road and Golf Road in Schertz.

Visitors need a valid ID and a sponsor with a DoD ID card; the Lindsey Visitor Center (Bldg. 1032, 1 Harmon Drive, 210-652-2838) is open weekdays 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. Holiday hours can change (JBSA's Veterans Day 2026 notice listed the East and West gates as closed, though the standing rule lists normal hours), so confirm on the official gate page before you go.

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-base family housing is Randolph Family Housing, owned and managed by Hunt Military Communities: four-bedroom duplexes and three- and four-bedroom single-family homes, more than 300 homes by Hunt's count. Rent equals your BAH at the with-dependents rate.
Waits change with the season, your rank and your bedroom entitlement, and EFMP status doesn't move you up. Military Housing Office: 610 Harmon Drive, (210) 652-1840.

source.label: DoD BAH Rate Lookup (MHA TX285, CY2026)

sections.title: Schools
data: On base, schooling is Randolph Field Independent School District (RFISD), a Texas public district on JBSA-Randolph with an elementary, middle and high school. It earned an A (94) in Texas's 2026 ratings. It is not a DoDEA district.

New students must live on base or hold an approved transfer. Transfers go by priority (military children living on other federal property first, then military children living off base, then children of civilians working on federal property, then of military retirees with 20 years of service), are limited by staffing, and are screened on grades, attendance and discipline. Questions: transfers@rfisd.net.

Off base, district lines don't follow town lines: Schertz-Cibolo-Universal City ISD (B, 81) and Judson ISD (C, 71) both list parts of Universal City, Schertz and Converse, and Comal ISD (B, 88) lists Garden Ridge and New Braunfels. Confirm the district for any address. School Liaison: 210-219-8025, jbsa.slo@us.af.mil.

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves, and the answer is mostly about how long you'll be here and how steady the local market is.
rent: Your tour is short (about two years or less) or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the area before committing to a neighborhood.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing when you PCS out.
Your BAH comfortably covers rent in the areas you'd consider.
buy: You expect to be here three or more years.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
The market is steady and you could rent the home out later if needed.
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length and the local market, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Check on-base availability and get the housing office's read on off-base neighborhoods before you sign anything.

steps.title: Register your vehicle and sort access
steps.text: Handle base access and vehicle registration, and learn the visitor-pass process for guests. Bring your registration and insurance.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Contact the gaining school district or DoDEA early and bring records and immunizations. The School Liaison Office can help with the transfer.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE region and enrollment so you can be seen at the local military treatment facility or network providers.

data.a: A flying-training base with a historic core around Building 100, the 'Taj Mahal', home to the 12th Flying Training Wing, HQ Air Education and Training Command, the Air Force Personnel Center and the Air Force Recruiting Service.

Universal City, Schertz, Converse and Cibolo are the close-in communities, split between Schertz-Cibolo-Universal City ISD and Judson ISD, so confirm the district for any address. On-base housing is Randolph Family Housing, run by Hunt Military Communities.

data.q: Is it far from the rest of San Antonio?
data.a: It sits northeast of the city. Brooke Army Medical Center on Fort Sam Houston is about 25 minutes away and Wilford Hall on Lackland about 42 with no traffic, JBSA's free base shuttles don't run at Randolph, and I-35 construction runs into the 2030s.
MHA TX285 (San Antonio), shared across JBSA. Use the calculator above.
